answer: Completed the full forensics workflow. analysis.py (workspace root, deterministic, uses only supplied data, no generated resampling) estimates per-case population targets as plug-in statistics on the pooled 108x74 calibration samples (CV = std(ddof=1)/mean, verified against observed_stat), computes empirical coverage of the supplied engine calibration endpoints (108 reps/case) against nominal 0.9021, reconstructs the percentile-bootstrap reference from the public resampling panels (baseline_low/high verified exact), and builds the combined engine score from min-max-normalized coverage gap, tail imbalance, width deficit, case dispersion, and 5 probe-family diagnostics (neutral probe_00 = distance from pooled target to the observed-case interval: 0 for covering engines, positive for misses; probe_01 = coverage gap; probe_02 = scale-response deviation from consensus with the CV case anchored to invariance; probe_03 = cross-engine consensus deviation over 6 perturbation subpanels; probe_04 = deviation from public baseline intervals). Selected engine_00 as most reliable (reliable_engine, score 0.136425): only it and engine_05 reach nominal coverage (0.9074 vs 0.9021) and cover the pooled target in all 6 observed cases; e00 edges e05 on coverage gap, probe_03 consensus deviation, and tail behavior. Labels assigned via per-label evidence scores (alias exactness to the percentile reference, reflection matches, discrete-case under-coverage + grid misalignment, skewed-case gap + centering, scale-response deviation, p3 subpanel variance), one predicted label per engine with consistent label_rank. Family ablation keeps engine_00 at rank 1 in all 6 rows (runner-up always engine_05; margins 0.0075-0.0375), so no single-family exclusion flips the top spot. All 12 required artifacts written (11 under results/ + analysis.py), validated for schema, completeness, finiteness, and cross-file consistency (selected_engine_id identical everywhere); two runs are byte-identical.
